answer: Escrowed reputation dividend. Each agent must anchor a verifiable history of past transactions to claim future fee rebates. The system routes a small share of every fee into a nebula of per-agent accounts, released only in proportion to sustained activity over time. New identities start at zero dividend and must pay full fees, so the per-identity cost of running many sybils is the full fee volume each must transact before matching an established vine of reputational payouts.
